title: The guard's cd walk resolves a `cd "$VAR"` target, so `cd "$R" && git worktree add` and `git -C "$R" worktree add` get the same verdict
why: Lane agent-worktree-add-in-tool-dir (session_013NEJL382EZLqWkzVvjj7UP), review round 2 of the variable-target follow-up, Nov 8 19:01 CST by triage's clock: `R=<primary>; cd "$R" && git worktree add /tmp/x`, run from cwd /tmp, is allowed, because hooks/guard_core.py dir_before_segment (about line 1057) drops a cd whose target holds a variable; the same add with `-C "$R"` is now refused on that lane's branch. Main allows both. Claude writes `cd "$X" && ...` in normal work.
note: dir_before_segment feeds many rules, so this needs its own lane and review, like resolve-vars-quote-split. Related: rm-after-cd-one-walk (todo) shares the same cd walk. The coordinator routes it. Routed by the coordinator, Nov 8 19:02 CST by triage's clock.
